headline.text: orders on time when suppliers write their dates vaguely (“next week”, “2-3 days late”): a plain date parser vs Sentinel, which plans for the latest reading and asks the supplier after a planner approves (p = 0.045; with exact dates it is 96.3%). A plain parser plans too early 54% of the time, Sentinel 1%. On 120 messages written blind by someone who never saw the code, its first run got 110 fully right and caught 49 of 51 ambiguous ones.
